=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple leaves clearly arise from the same central point at the stem apex in a radial pattern)

B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (leaf blades are undivided and attached directly to the stem)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology

    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): oblanceolate (leaf is broadest above the middle and tapers towards the base)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acuminate (tapering to a distinct, elongated tip)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (tapering gradually to the petiole)

D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (indicates a lignified structure typical of tree seedlings)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (stem appears smooth)
    19. Stem color: brownish-green (visible in the close-up image near the leaf attachment points)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits

F. Notes: The leaves are arranged in a dense terminal whorl. The venation is very prominent, giving the leaf surface a somewhat rugose or blistered appearance between the veins. An orange tag is present on the stem, likely for identification purposes.
